title: RL2: A Call for Simultaneous Representation Learning and Rule Learning for Graph Streams

problem.claim: Graph-stream applications commonly involve heterogeneous graph data.

gap.claim: Representation learning supports prediction but is limited for interpretation and reasoning, motivating combination with rule learning.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes RL2, a system for jointly performing representation learning and rule learning from one online graph-stream training process.
The proposed approach combines connectionist representation learning with symbolic rule learning.
The learned rules are intended to support interpretation and construction of dynamic Bayesian networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report analytical and empirical evidence that the system is efficient and responsive for graph streams.
The authors report good prediction accuracy for representation learning.
The authors report that the system returns high-quality rules for interpretation and dynamic Bayesian network construction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Heterogeneous graph streams are presented as common in current applications.
Representation learning is described as accurate for prediction but weak in interpretation and reasoning.
The paper motivates coexistence of connectionist networks and symbolic rules to address their respective deficiencies.
The proposed goal is simultaneous, efficient learning of representations and rules during online graph-stream training.
RL2 is reported to perform well on efficiency, responsiveness, prediction, and rule quality.

source_observation.claim: The approach learns representations and rules together from the same online training process.

interpretation.claim: Combining predictive representation learning with symbolic rules may address both performance and interpretability needs.

application.claim: Use joint representation-and-rule learning when streaming graph systems require both prediction and interpretable reasoning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this tradeoff holds across graph-stream domains or under specific operational constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the learning algorithm, model architecture, or rule representation.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or evaluation conditions.
The abstract does not describe computational-resource requirements or scalability limits.
